title: In My Hands: Compelling Stories from a Surgeon and His Patients Fighting Cancer
author: Steven A. Curley, MD
target_audience: Individuals affected by cancer (patients, survivors, families)
Readers interested in memoirs of doctors
General readers seeking insight into the human side of medicine
Advocates and supporters of cancer research
core_themes: The emotional and ethical challenges of surgery
Hope, loss, and the search for meaning in illness
primary_purpose: To share moving, real-life stories from the front lines of cancer surgery, highlighting the deep connections between a surgeon and his patients, and to reveal the emotional and ethical complexities of confronting cancer in the operating room and beyond.

structure_format.organization: Collection of individual patient stories interwoven with the author's own experiences and insights

key_concepts_lessons: Medicine is as much about human connection as it is about technical skill.
Every patient’s journey is unique and deserving of respect and empathy.
Physicians are profoundly impacted by their patients’ stories of survival and loss.
Surgical decisions entail ethical considerations that affect lives.
Hope can thrive even in the face of devastating diagnoses.
The importance of compassion and communication in patient care.
notable_features: True patient narratives with personal reflections from a seasoned cancer surgeon
Medical information conveyed in an accessible, non-technical manner
Balanced exploration of both triumphs and tragedies
Addresses both the science and humanity of cancer care
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2020s, against a backdrop of increased patient advocacy, advances in cancer treatment, and a growing public interest in humanizing the medical profession. The book aligns with contemporary conversations about empathy and resilience in healthcare.
reception_impact: Received positive reviews for its candid, moving storytelling
Appreciated by medical professionals and lay readers alike
Praised for conveying the complexity and emotionality of cancer care
Recognized as a resource for those affected by cancer seeking connection and understanding
comparable_titles: When Breath Becomes Air by Paul Kalanithi
The Emperor of All Maladies by Siddhartha Mukherjee
What Patients Say, What Doctors Hear by Danielle Ofri
